To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the leukemic cells of individuals with CLL express IL-7 and that a portion of the T cells and some non-T,non-B cells also express the IL-7 receptor.
IL-7 mRNA and IL-7 receptors are expressed in CLL cells and that IL-7 receptor bearing cells are present in the peripheral blood of patients with CLL.
IL-7 expression is aberrantly regulated in the leukemic cells of CLL patients and that the leukemic cells express the IL-7 receptor.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the role of cytokine expression in the regulation of growth of leukemic cells in CLL.
the role of cytokines in the pathogenesis of CLL and the regulation of expression of the genes encoding these cytokines.
the regulation of expression of IL-7 in leukemic cells of individuals with CLL.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the IL-7 gene is aberrantly regulated in CLL, and that IL-7 is expressed in the leukemic cells of CLL patients.
in chronic lymphocytic leukemic patients, IL-7 expression is restricted to the leukemic cells and is not found in the normal nonleukemic cells of the same individuals.
the expression of IL-7 mRNA in the leukemic cells of CLL patients is a result of the aberrant expression of this gene in a subset of leukemic cells.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
IL-7 is expressed by the leukemic cells of CLL patients and not by the normal cells.
the leukemic cells of CLL patients express IL-7 receptors and are capable of responding to IL-7.
IL-7 is expressed in the leukemic cell subset in patients with CLL.
The main takeaway from our work is that
IL-7 is expressed in leukemic cell populations of patients with CLL, but not in the nonleukemic cell subsets.
IL-7 expression is not normal in chronic lymphocytic leukemic patients.
the leukemic cells from the CLL cases that we studied expressed IL-7 mRNA and the receptor for IL-7.
